qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Infrastructure construction contracting operates under competitive fixed-price bidding with thin operating margins (3-6%) and persistent exposure to cost overruns. The energy division (Acciona Energía) generates power from wind and solar farms, selling an undifferentiated commodity into wholesale merchant power markets that suffer from renewable price cannibalization (capture price erosion during high wind/solar output). Consolidated group ROIC is chronically depressed at ~2-4%, failing the 12% hurdle, with no pricing power >= inflation.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (Proof of Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). Conglomerate spanning civil engineering construction contracting and merchant renewable energy generation (Acciona Energía). Construction faces cyclical competitive bidding and cost overruns, while renewable power sells commodity electrons exposed to power price drops and negative capture pricing. Consolidated ROIC is structurally sub-hurdle (~2-4%), failing to cover its cost of capital.
qualitative.evidence: Consolidated EBITDA grew to €2.5B in 2024 and €3.2B in 2025 aided by asset rotations at Acciona Energía and turnaround at Nordex, with Net Debt of €7.0B (~2.2x-2.9x EBITDA). However, multi-cycle group ROIC remains severely depressed at 1.8%-3.5%, consistently below WACC (~6.5%). The merchant power segment lacks pricing power against wholesale power price declines and Spanish regulatory windfall interventions, while the infrastructure division operates in high-risk lump-sum EPC contracts.
